sections.name: File setup (part 1)
sections.title: Package description and imports
sections.what: Describes the app and sets the version number. Then it brings in the data shapes, the search engine, the agents, the utilities, the visualizer and the exporters.
sections.why: Collects the main pieces in one place so callers can reach them through the package.
sections.watch_out: A renamed item in any of these imported files will break the whole package.

sections.name: File setup (part 2)
sections.title: Public names list
sections.what: Lists the names this package makes public, grouped as data models, core components, utilities, visualizations and exports.
sections.why: Likely reason: this list controls which names are shared when someone uses a star import, and it helps documentation tools find the public parts.
sections.watch_out: A name listed here but not imported causes an error for star imports, and a name imported but not listed is hidden from them.

summary: This is the front door of the package. It gathers the main parts from the other files so other code can import them from one place.
purpose: Lists what the Proposal Builder package offers to the rest of the program and to outside callers.
why: Likely reason: callers can write one import line instead of needing to know which file holds each piece.
how: First it describes the app and sets the version number. Then it imports the data shapes, the search engine, the agents, the utilities, the visualizer and the exporters. Last, it lists the public names in the export list.
inputs: No direct inputs. It reads the modules it imports from other files.
outputs: When another program imports this package, it gets the listed classes and functions, and the version number.
risks: If any imported file is missing or renames a class or function, importing this package fails for every caller. Importing it also loads all of the program's dependencies at once, so a missing library breaks it too.
debug: Read the error message to find the file it names. Check that the named file exists and defines that name. Then check that the required libraries are installed.
